q.t: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
q.e: Two join the midpoints of opposite sides and two are the diagonals. Folding along any of them makes the halves match.

q.t: How many lines of symmetry does an equilateral triangle have?
q.e: One from each vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side.

q.t: How many lines of symmetry does a circle have?
q.e: Every line through the centre (every diameter) folds the circle onto itself, and there is no end to the diameters.

q.t: How many lines of symmetry does the capital letter A have?
q.e: Only the vertical line down the middle — the left and right halves are mirror images.

q.t: How many lines of symmetry does a rectangle (that is not a square) have?
q.e: The two lines joining midpoints of opposite sides. The diagonals do NOT work — folding along one leaves corners sticking out.

q.t: What is the order of rotational symmetry of a square?
q.e: In one full turn it looks the same 4 times — after 90°, 180°, 270° and 360°.

q.t: In a mirror placed beside it, the letter p looks like:
q.e: A mirror swaps left and right but not up and down, so the loop moves to the other side of the stick: q.

q.t: How many lines of symmetry does an isosceles triangle (not equilateral) have?
q.e: Only the line from the vertex between the equal sides to the midpoint of the base.

q.t: Which of these capital letters has NO line of symmetry?
q.e: A and M fold left-to-right, H folds both ways. F matches under no fold.

q.t: How many lines of symmetry does a regular hexagon have?
q.e: A regular polygon with n sides has n lines of symmetry: 3 through opposite corners and 3 through midpoints of opposite sides.

q.t: What is the order of rotational symmetry of an equilateral triangle?
q.e: It fits onto itself after turns of 120°, 240° and 360° — three times in a full turn.

q.t: What is the smallest angle through which a square can be turned to look the same (in degrees)?
Which capital letter has both a horizontal and a vertical line of symmetry?
q.e: H folds top-to-bottom and left-to-right. A and M only fold left-to-right; B only top-to-bottom.

q.t: How many lines of symmetry does a parallelogram (not a rectangle or rhombus) have?
q.e: No fold makes the halves match — the slanted sides land in the wrong places.

q.t: What is the order of rotational symmetry of a parallelogram?
q.e: A half-turn (180°) about the point where the diagonals cross puts it back onto itself.

q.t: How many lines of symmetry does a rhombus (not a square) have?
q.e: Its two diagonals. All four sides are equal, so folding along a diagonal matches the sides.

q.t: How many lines of symmetry does a regular pentagon have?
q.e: One through each vertex and the midpoint of the opposite side — 5 in all.

q.t: What is the angle of rotational symmetry of a regular hexagon (in degrees)?
The capital letter S has:
o: Rotational symmetry of order 2 but no line of symmetry
q.e: No fold matches its halves, but a half-turn brings it back onto itself.

q.t: How many lines of symmetry does a scalene triangle have?
q.e: With all sides different, no fold can make two matching halves.

q.t: A figure has rotational symmetry of order 4. What is its angle of rotation (in degrees)?
q.e: Angle = 360° ÷ order = 90°.

q.t: A regular polygon has an angle of rotational symmetry of 40°. How many sides does it have?
q.e: Order = 360 ÷ 40 = 9, and a regular polygon’s order equals its number of sides.

q.t: How many lines of symmetry does a kite have?
q.e: Only the diagonal that joins the two corners where the equal sides meet.

q.t: What is the order of rotational symmetry of the capital letter Z?
q.e: A half-turn brings Z back onto itself; a quarter-turn makes it look like N.

q.t: Which shape has line symmetry but NO rotational symmetry (other than a full turn)?
q.e: An isosceles triangle folds along one line, but only a full 360° turn brings it back.

q.t: Which shape has rotational symmetry but NO line of symmetry?
q.e: A parallelogram fits itself after a half-turn (order 2) but cannot be folded into matching halves.

q.t: How many lines of symmetry does a regular polygon with 12 sides have?
q.e: A regular n-sided polygon has n lines of symmetry.

q.t: How many lines of symmetry does a semicircle have?
q.e: Only the line through the middle of the straight edge, at right angles to it.

q.t: A clock shows 3 o’clock. What time does it appear to show in a mirror?
q.e: The mirror swaps left and right, so the hour hand pointing right at 3 appears to point left at 9.

q.t: A figure has rotational symmetry of order 5. Find its angle of rotation (in degrees).
Can a figure have 50° as its smallest angle of rotational symmetry?
o: No, because 50 does not divide 360 exactly
q.e: Repeating the turn must bring the figure back exactly at 360°. 360 ÷ 50 = 7.2 is not a whole number.

q.t: A figure’s smallest angle of rotational symmetry is 45°. What is its order?
How many letters of the word MATHS (in capitals) have at least one line of symmetry?
q.e: M, A and T fold left-to-right; H folds both ways. S has no line of symmetry. That is 4 letters.

q.t: How many letters of the word ZOOM (in capitals) have rotational symmetry of order more than 1?
q.e: Z looks the same after a half-turn, and so does each O. M turned upside down becomes W. That is 3 letters.

q.t: A clock seen in a mirror appears to show 4:20. What is the real time?
q.e: Mirror time and real time add up to 12:00 (written as 11:60). 11:60 − 4:20 = 7:40.

q.t: A regular polygon has rotational symmetry of order 10. What is the size of each of its exterior angles (in degrees)?
q.e: It has 10 sides, and the exterior angles of any polygon total 360°: 360 ÷ 10 = 36°. This equals its angle of rotation.

q.t: Which shape has exactly 2 lines of symmetry AND rotational symmetry of order 2?
q.e: Rectangle: 2 lines, order 2. Square: 4 and 4. Parallelogram: 0 lines. Equilateral triangle: 3 and 3.

q.t: Which number reads exactly the same after a half-turn (180°)?
q.e: A half-turn swaps the two digits’ places and turns 6 into 9 and 9 into 6: 69 → 69. (66 becomes 99, 68 becomes 89, 19 becomes 61.)

q.t: Add up the lines of symmetry of a square, a rectangle and an equilateral triangle.
A regular polygon has 8 lines of symmetry. Find its angle of rotational symmetry (in degrees).
q.e: 8 lines of symmetry means 8 sides and order 8: 360 ÷ 8 = 45°.
